protocol.evidence: The three held-out CHO deliveries of the offline trial, shared as provisional evidence; every arm starts from a fresh application holding the same deliveries.

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

**glucose**, CHO-004-R02 minus CHO-004-R01: 11 matching measured times from 0 h to 142 h. Largest difference -0.944 g/L at 19.5 h (6.189 against 7.133 g/L); mean difference -0.2392 g/L.

rows.text: Why is glucose different between CHO-004-R01 and CHO-004-R02?

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
A cause is not established in the records I can see. What the data shows: glucose in CHO-004-R02 runs slightly below CHO-004-R01 at almost every matched sample time, with the largest gap of **−0.94 g/L at 19.5 h (R01 7.133 vs R02 6.189)**; the only times R02 is higher are the start (7.072 vs 6.897 at 0 h) and 28 h (6.689 vs 6.428). Across the 11 exact-time matches (0–142 h), the mean difference is −0.24 g/L with 9 of 11 samples lower in R02, and both runs follow the same shape, decaying from ~7 g/L to under 1 g/L by the end — so R02 looks like a slightly faster-consuming or under-fed run, but nothing in the records pins down why.

Two caveats matter here:

- **No context is recorded**: product, process version, equipment, scale and process stage are all "not recorded" for both batches in the Northfield Biologics October delivery (provisional, values still in review — verification has 55 open checks). Without that, a difference between runs made under possibly different conditions cannot be attributed; the compare result itself flags "causal claim not supported."
- **Only these glucose series exist**: I searched for linked records on both batch IDs and found nothing else at this site — no batch, case, deviation or procedure records, and no maintenance or calibration evidence — so I did not find any documented cause in the records I searched.

Both series continue past this comparison only in R01 (an unmatched 164 h sample, 0.124 g/L), so the runs also differ slightly in length. What would settle it: comparing **feed added and viable cell density** between the two runs in the same delivery (a higher consumption rate vs less feed), and getting the run context (equipment, process version) from the CMO records. The comparison values I used are unreviewed.

rows.text: Why is glucose different between CHO-007-R01 and CHO-007-R02?

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
No cause is established in the records I can see — that's the honest headline. Neither run has a batch record, case, deviation or specification here; the only source is the Northfield Biologics · November CMO delivery, and it records no product, process version, equipment, scale or process stage for either run. So the workspace cannot say *why* they differ; it can only show how.

**What the measurements show** (glucose, g/L, offline LIMS samples; times are elapsed hours): the runs start essentially together — 7.618 (CHO-007-R01) vs 7.684 (CHO-007-R02) at 0 h — and then CHO-007-R02 sits at or below CHO-007-R01 at **every** matched time from 18 h to 146 h (8 of 9 samples lower). The largest gap is at 18 h: 7.83 vs 7.275, i.e. 0.555 g/L lower; mean difference −0.207 g/L, root-mean-square 0.276 g/L (descriptive only — successive samples of one run aren't independent). The one-directional, run-long pattern is consistent with CHO-007-R02 consuming/depleting glucose faster (higher cell uptake or a slightly different feed trajectory), but that is an inference from the trend, not a finding from any record.

**Caveats before leaning on this**
- The delivery is still **in review**: 79 open checks, values read from the files and not yet accepted. Notably, CHO-007-R02 glucose at 44 h has two conflicting source rows awaiting review, which is why CHO-007-R01's 44 h sample (6.957 g/L) was excluded from the matched comparison.
- Glucose comes from offline LIMS samples (roughly 8–30 h apart), while feed volume and other process trends are ~6 h online samples, so short-term swings between samples aren't resolved.

**What would settle it:** review of the conflicting 44 h rows and the delivery's missing batch-document check, plus Northfield's batch documentation (equipment, scale, feed profile, setpoints) — none of that is in this workspace yet. Comparing feed added and viable cell density between the two runs from the same delivery would be the first data-side check once the delivery is verified.

rows.text: Why is glucose different between CHO-010-R01 and CHO-010-R02?

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
The Harborview CDMO fed-batch summary (still in review — 842 values pending, none rejected) shows the two runs' glucose tracks closely early on and then splits late in the culture, but the records I can see do not say **why**: no batch record, case or investigation exists for CHO-010-R01 or CHO-010-R02, and product, process version, equipment, scale and stage are all not recorded in the comparison context.

**What the data shows** (glucose, g/L, at matched elapsed hours; R02 minus R01):

- **0–117 h: nearly identical.** Differences wobble between −0.28 and +0.15 g/L around a mean of roughly ±0.1 g/L (e.g. at 17.5 h: 6.74 vs 6.61; at 117 h: 4.93 vs 4.89).
- **140–209 h: R02 consistently higher.** Every matched sample from 140 h on is higher in R02: +0.47 g/L at 140 h (4.80 vs 5.27), +0.57 g/L at 160.5 h (3.86 vs 4.43), +0.45 g/L at 169 h (3.61 vs 4.06), and the largest gap **+1.15 g/L at 193.5 h (R01 2.72 vs R02 3.87)**.
- Late-phase shape differs too: R01's glucose drops steeply after 185.5 h, while R02 holds up at 193.5 h and only falls at 209 h (1.11 vs 1.74); R02 also runs 8.5 h longer, with a final sample at 217.5 h (1.09 g/L) that has no match in R01.

**What that means:** the persistent late-phase offset is real in the data but its cause is not established. A plausible hypothesis is lower glucose consumption in R02 — a smaller or slower-growing cell population would deplete glucose more slowly — since the divergence starts while R01's glucose is falling fastest; alternatively R02 received more feed late in the run. I did not find anything in the records to confirm or rule these out: the delivery includes feed added and viable cell density but this comparison covered glucose only, and no case, deviation or batch record names either run. Reviewing the delivery first is the right order anyway — the numbers above are all still in review (54 open MISSING_FIELD checks on the package), so treat them as unconfirmed.

What would settle it: a same-style matched-time comparison of **feed added and viable cell density** for these two runs across 140–209 h, plus the batch context (equipment, scale, process version) that the context check shows is not recorded here.
